# Suzent

> Suzent is a sovereign AI agent: an open-source, local-first agent whose identity, memory, skills, workspace, and runtime remain under the user's control. Models are replaceable; the agent is not.

A sovereign AI agent is an AI agent whose identity, memory, skills, workspace, and runtime are owned and governed by its user rather than by a model provider or platform. Its durable state lives in files the user can read, edit, version, and move; its actions run inside permission boundaries the user defines; and replacing the underlying model does not reset the agent. Suzent is an implementation of that definition.

Full text of this documentation, in one file: https://suzent.com/llms-full.txt

## Start here

- [What is a sovereign AI agent?](https://suzent.com/sovereign): The definition, the four conditions of agent sovereignty, and a five-question ownership test.
- [Introduction](https://suzent.com/docs/getting-started/intro): What Suzent is and how it differs from a rented AI account.
- [Quickstart](https://suzent.com/docs/getting-started/quickstart): Install and run Suzent.

## Sovereignty architecture

- [Memory](https://suzent.com/docs/concepts/memory): Sovereign continuity — readable, file-backed memory where the index serves the files.
- [Human in the loop](https://suzent.com/docs/concepts/tools/human-in-the-loop): Sovereign authority — approval boundaries for tool execution.
- [Filesystem](https://suzent.com/docs/concepts/filesystem): Sovereign vessel — controlled workspaces and filesystem access.
- [GitHub sync](https://suzent.com/docs/concepts/github-sync): Sovereign continuity — portable agent state with credentials kept local.
- [Automation](https://suzent.com/docs/concepts/automation): Goals, schedules, and continuing work.
- [Nodes](https://suzent.com/docs/concepts/nodes): Extending the agent across approved devices.
